gcode_comments.label: Verbose G-code
gcode_comments.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

infill_combination.label: Infill combination
infill_combination.tooltip: Automatically combine sparse infill of several layers to print together in order to reduce time. Walls are still printed with original layer height.

infill_shift_step.label: Infill shift step
infill_shift_step.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

sparse_infill_rotate_template.label: Sparse infill rotation template
sparse_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

solid_infill_rotate_template.label: Solid infill rotation template
solid_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

skeleton_infill_density.label: Skeleton infill density
skeleton_infill_density.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

skin_infill_density.label: Skin infill density
skin_infill_density.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

skin_infill_depth.label: Skin infill depth
skin_infill_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

infill_lock_depth.label: Infill lock depth
infill_lock_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

skin_infill_line_width.label: Skin line width
skin_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

skeleton_infill_line_width.label: Skeleton line width
skeleton_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

symmetric_infill_y_axis.label: Symmetric infill Y axis
symmetric_infill_y_axis.tooltip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the Y axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

infill_combination_max_layer_height.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
infill_combination_max_layer_height.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

lateral_lattice_angle_1.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
lateral_lattice_angle_1.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

lateral_lattice_angle_2.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
lateral_lattice_angle_2.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

infill_overhang_angle.label: Infill overhang angle
infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

lightning_overhang_angle.label: Lightning overhang angle
lightning_overhang_angle.tooltip: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.

lightning_prune_angle.label: Prune angle
lightning_prune_angle.tooltip:
Controls how aggressively short or unsupported Lightning branches are pruned.
This angle is converted internally to a per-layer distance.

lightning_straightening_angle.label: Straightening angle
lightning_straightening_angle.tooltip: Maximum straightening angle used to simplify Lightning branches.

infill_anchor.label: Sparse infill anchor length
infill_anchor.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

sparse_infill_filament_id.label: Infill
sparse_infill_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print internal sparse infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

sparse_infill_line_width.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

infill_wall_overlap.label: Infill/wall overlap
infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: This allows the infill area to be enlarged slightly to overlap with walls for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimizing the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill.

sparse_infill_speed.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for internal sparse infill.

interface_shells.label: Interface shells
interface_shells.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

mmu_segmented_region_max_width.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_max_width.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. A value of 0 disables this feature.

mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth" is bigger than "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

interlocking_beam.label: Use beam interlocking
interlocking_beam.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

interlocking_beam_width.label: Interlocking beam width
interlocking_beam_width.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

interlocking_beam_layer_count.label: Interlocking beam layers
interlocking_beam_layer_count.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth
interlocking_depth.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

interlocking_boundary_avoidance.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
interlocking_boundary_avoidance.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

ironing_type.label: Ironing type
ironing_type.tooltip: Ironing uses a small flow to print at the same height of a surface to make flat surfaces smoother. This setting controls which layers are being ironed.

ironing_pattern.label: Ironing Pattern
ironing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
ironing_flow.tooltip: This is the amount of material to be extruded during ironing. It is relative to the flow of normal layer height. Too high a value will result in overextrusion on the surface.

ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
ironing_spacing.tooltip: This is the distance between the lines used for ironing.

ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
ironing_inset.tooltip: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
ironing_speed.tooltip: This is the print speed for ironing lines.

ironing_angle.label: Ironing angle offset
ironing_angle.tooltip: The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.

ironing_angle_fixed.label: Fixed ironing angle
ironing_angle_fixed.tooltip: Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.

ironing_expansion.label: Ironing expansion
ironing_expansion.tooltip: Expand or contract the ironing area.

zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.label: Minimize wall height angle
zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.tooltip:
Reduce the height of top-surface perimeters to match the model edge height.
Affects perimeters with a slope less than this angle (degrees).
A reasonable value is 35. Set to 0 to disable.

zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.label: Don't alternate fill direction
zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.tooltip: Disable alternating fill direction when using Z contouring.

zaa_min_z.label: Minimum Z height
zaa_min_z.tooltip:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.

layer_change_gcode.label: Layer change G-code
layer_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

silent_mode.label: Silent Mode
silent_mode.tooltip: Whether the machine supports silent mode in which machine uses lower acceleration to print more quietly

emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.label: Emit limits to G-code
emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

machine_pause_gcode.label: Pause G-code
machine_pause_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

template_custom_gcode.label: Custom G-code
template_custom_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
small_area_infill_flow_compensation.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.label: Flow Compensation Model
small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factor. Each pair is on a separate line, followed by a semicolon, in the following format: "1.234, 5.678;"

machine_max_junction_deviation.tooltip:
Maximum junction deviation (M205 J, only apply if JD > 0 for Marlin Firmware
If your Marlin 2 printer uses Classic Jerk set this value to 0.)

machine_max_force_Y.full_label: Maximum force of the Y axis
machine_max_force_Y.tooltip: The allowed maximum output force of Y axis

machine_bed_mass_Y.full_label: Bed mass of the Y axis
machine_bed_mass_Y.tooltip: The machine bed mass load of Y axis

machine_max_printed_mass.tooltip: The allowed max printed mass on a plate

machine_max_acceleration_travel.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for travel (M204 T), it only applies to Marlin 2.

resonance_avoidance.label: Resonance avoidance
resonance_avoidance.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

input_shaping_emit.label: Emit input shaping
input_shaping_emit.tooltip:
Override firmware input shaping settings.
If disabled, firmware settings are used.

input_shaping_type.label: Input shaper type
input_shaping_type.tooltip:
Choose the input shaper algorithm.
Default uses the firmware default settings.
Disable turns off input shaping in the firmware.

input_shaping_freq_x.label: X
input_shaping_freq_x.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_freq_y.label: Y
input_shaping_freq_y.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

input_shaping_damp_x.label: X
input_shaping_damp_x.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_damp_y.label: Y
input_shaping_damp_y.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

fan_max_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_max_speed.tooltip: The part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

max_layer_height.label: Max
max_layer_height.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.label: Smoothing segment length
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.label: Apply only on external features
extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.tooltip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

fan_min_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_min_speed.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

additional_cooling_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
additional_cooling_fan_speed.tooltip:
Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)

close_additional_fan_first_x_layers.label: For the first
close_additional_fan_first_x_layers.tooltip: Set special auxiliary cooling fan for the first certain layers.

additional_fan_full_speed_layer.label: Full fan speed at layer
additional_fan_full_speed_layer.tooltip:
Auxiliary fan speed will be ramped up linearly from layer "For the first" to maximum at layer "Full fan speed at layer".
"Full fan speed at layer" will be ignored if lower than "For the first", in which case the fan will run at maximum allowed speed at layer "For the first" + 1.

first_x_layer_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
first_x_layer_fan_speed.tooltip: Special auxiliary cooling fan speed, effective only for the first x layers.

min_layer_height.label: Min
min_layer_height.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

slow_down_min_speed.label: Min print speed
slow_down_min_speed.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

notes.label: Configuration notes
notes.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

host_type.label: Host Type
host_type.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field must contain the kind of the host.

nozzle_volume.label: Nozzle volume
nozzle_volume.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the filament cutter and the end of the nozzle

cooling_tube_retraction.label: Cooling tube position
cooling_tube_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

cooling_tube_length.label: Cooling tube length
cooling_tube_length.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

high_current_on_filament_swap.label: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

parking_pos_retraction.label: Filament parking position
parking_pos_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

extra_loading_move.label: Extra loading distance
extra_loading_move.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

start_end_points.label: Start end points
start_end_points.tooltip: The start and end points which are from the cutter area to the excess chute.

reduce_infill_retraction.label: Reduce infill retraction
reduce_infill_retraction.tooltip: Don\'t retract when the travel is entirely within an infill area. That means the oozing can\'t been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower. Note that z-hop is also not performed in areas where retraction is skipped.

ooze_prevention.label: Enable
ooze_prevention.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

filename_format.label: Filename format
filename_format.tooltip: Users can decide project file names when exporting.

make_overhang_printable.label: Make overhangs printable
make_overhang_printable.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

make_overhang_printable_angle.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
make_overhang_printable_angle.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

make_overhang_printable_hole_size.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
make_overhang_printable_hole_size.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

detect_overhang_wall.label: Detect overhang walls
detect_overhang_wall.tooltip: This detects the overhang percentage relative to line width and uses a different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridging speed is used.

outer_wall_filament_id.label: Outer walls
outer_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print outer walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

inner_wall_filament_id.label: Inner walls
inner_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

inner_wall_line_width.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

inner_wall_speed.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for inner walls.

wall_loops.label: Wall loops
wall_loops.tooltip: This is the number of walls per layer.

alternate_extra_wall.label: Alternate extra wall
alternate_extra_wall.tooltip:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

post_process.label: Post-processing Scripts
post_process.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Orca Slicer config settings by reading environment variables.

process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code (process)
process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed. It runs after the machine and filament extrusion role G-code.

plugins.label: Plugins Used
plugins.tooltip: Plugin capabilities referenced by this preset, stored as name;uuid;capability.

slicing_pipeline_plugin.label: Slicing Pipeline Plugin
slicing_pipeline_plugin.tooltip: Python plugin(s) invoked at each slicing pipeline step to read and modify intermediate slicing data, including a final G-code post-processing step. Research/experimental.

printer_notes.label: Printer notes
printer_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

raft_contact_distance.label: Raft contact Z distance
raft_contact_distance.tooltip: Z gap between raft and object. If Support Top Z Distance is 0, this value is ignored and the object is printed in direct contact with the raft (no gap).

raft_expansion.label: Raft expansion
raft_expansion.tooltip: This expands all raft layers in XY plane.

raft_first_layer_density.label: First layer density
raft_first_layer_density.tooltip: This is the density of the first raft or support layer.

raft_first_layer_expansion.label: First layer expansion
raft_first_layer_expansion.tooltip: This expands the first raft or support layer to improve bed adhesion.

raft_layers.label: Raft layers
raft_layers.tooltip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.tooltip: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller values mean higher resolution and more time required to slice.

retraction_minimum_travel.label: Travel distance threshold
retraction_minimum_travel.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
retract_before_wipe.tooltip: This is the length of fast retraction before a wipe, relative to retraction length.

retract_after_wipe.label: Retract amount after wipe
retract_after_wipe.tooltip:
The length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

retract_when_changing_layer.label: Retract on layer change
retract_when_changing_layer.tooltip: This forces a retraction on layer changes.

retraction_length.label: Length
retraction_length.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

long_retractions_when_cut.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
long_retractions_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

retraction_distances_when_cut.label: Retraction distance when cut
retraction_distances_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

z_hop.label: Z-hop height
z_hop.tooltip: Whenever there is a retraction, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from hitting the print when traveling more. Using spiral lines to lift z can prevent stringing.

retract_lift_above.label: Only lift Z above
retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

retract_lift_below.label: Only lift Z below
retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

travel_slope.label: Traveling angle
travel_slope.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

retract_lift_enforce.label: On surfaces
retract_lift_enforce.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

extruder_type.label: Type
extruder_type.tooltip: This setting is only used for initial value of manual calibration of pressure advance. Bowden extruder usually has larger PA value. This setting doesn't influence normal slicing.

default_nozzle_volume_type.label: Default Nozzle Volume Type.
default_nozzle_volume_type.tooltip: Default Nozzle volume type for extruders in this printer.

extruder_nozzle_stats.label: Extruder nozzle stats
extruder_nozzle_stats.tooltip: Physical nozzle counts per extruder, keyed by nozzle volume type.

extruder_nozzle_volume_type.label: Extruder nozzle volume type
extruder_nozzle_volume_type.tooltip: Nozzle volume type per physical nozzle of an extruder.

enable_filament_dynamic_map.label: Enable filament dynamic map
enable_filament_dynamic_map.tooltip: Enable dynamic filament mapping during print.

has_filament_switcher.label: Has filament switcher
has_filament_switcher.tooltip: Printer has a filament switcher hardware (e.g., AMS).

master_extruder_id.label: Master extruder id
master_extruder_id.tooltip: Default extruder id to place filament.

retract_restart_extra.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

retract_restart_extra_toolchange.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra_toolchange.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

retraction_speed.label: Retraction speed
retraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

deretraction_speed.label: Deretraction speed
deretraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

deretract_speed_extruder_change.label: Deretraction speed (extruder change)
deretract_speed_extruder_change.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle when switching extruder.

use_firmware_retraction.label: Use firmware retraction
use_firmware_retraction.tooltip: This experimental setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

disable_m73.label: Disable set remaining print time
disable_m73.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

seam_position.label: Seam position
seam_position.tooltip: This is the starting position for each part of the outer wall.

staggered_inner_seams.label: Staggered inner seams
staggered_inner_seams.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

seam_gap.label: Seam gap
seam_gap.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

seam_slope_type.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
seam_slope_type.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

seam_slope_conditional.label: Conditional scarf joint
seam_slope_conditional.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

scarf_angle_threshold.label: Conditional angle threshold
scarf_angle_threshold.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

scarf_overhang_threshold.label: Conditional overhang threshold
scarf_overhang_threshold.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

scarf_joint_speed.label: Scarf joint speed
scarf_joint_speed.tooltip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

scarf_joint_flow_ratio.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
scarf_joint_flow_ratio.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

seam_slope_start_height.label: Scarf start height
seam_slope_start_height.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

seam_slope_entire_loop.label: Scarf around entire wall
seam_slope_entire_loop.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

seam_slope_min_length.label: Scarf length
seam_slope_min_length.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

seam_slope_steps.label: Scarf steps
seam_slope_steps.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

seam_slope_inner_walls.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
seam_slope_inner_walls.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

role_based_wipe_speed.label: Role base wipe speed
role_based_wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

wipe_on_loops.label: Wipe on loops
wipe_on_loops.tooltip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

wipe_before_external_loop.label: Wipe before external loop
wipe_before_external_loop.tooltip:
To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.

This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely an external perimeter is printed immediately after a de-retraction move.

wipe_speed.label: Wipe speed
wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above. The default value for this parameter is 80%.

skirt_distance.label: Skirt distance
skirt_distance.tooltip: This is the distance from the skirt to the brim or the object.

skirt_start_angle.label: Skirt start point
skirt_start_angle.tooltip: Angle from the object center to skirt start point. Zero is the most right position, counter clockwise is positive angle.

skirt_height.label: Skirt height
skirt_height.tooltip: Number of skirt layers: usually only one

single_loop_draft_shield.label: Single loop after first layer
single_loop_draft_shield.tooltip: Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.

draft_shield.label: Draft shield
draft_shield.tooltip:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. Otherwise 'Skirt height' is used.
Note: With the draft shield active, the skirt will be printed at skirt distance from the object. Therefore, if brims are active it may intersect with them. To avoid this, increase the skirt distance value.

skirt_type.label: Skirt type
skirt_type.tooltip: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

skirt_loops.label: Skirt loops
skirt_loops.tooltip: This is the number of loops for the skirt. 0 means the skirt is disabled.

skirt_speed.label: Skirt speed
skirt_speed.tooltip: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

min_skirt_length.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
min_skirt_length.tooltip:
Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled.

Using a non-zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.
Final number of loops is not taking into account while arranging or validating objects distance. Increase loop number in such case.

slow_down_layer_time.label: Layer time
slow_down_layer_time.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

minimum_sparse_infill_area.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
minimum_sparse_infill_area.tooltip: Sparse infill areas which are smaller than this threshold value are replaced by internal solid infill.

internal_solid_filament_id.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print internal solid infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

top_surface_filament_id.label: Top surface
top_surface_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print top surface.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

bottom_surface_filament_id.label: Bottom surface
bottom_surface_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print bottom surface.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

internal_solid_infill_line_width.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

internal_solid_infill_speed.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for internal solid infill, not including the top or bottom surface.

spiral_mode.label: Spiral vase
spiral_mode.tooltip: This enables spiraling, which smooths out the Z moves of the outer contour and turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

spiral_mode_smooth.label: Smooth Spiral
spiral_mode_smooth.tooltip: Smooth Spiral smooths out X and Y moves as well, resulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical.

spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing.label: Max XY Smoothing
spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing.tooltip: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiral. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

spiral_starting_flow_ratio.label: Spiral starting flow ratio
spiral_starting_flow_ratio.tooltip: Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

spiral_finishing_flow_ratio.label: Spiral finishing flow ratio
spiral_finishing_flow_ratio.tooltip: Sets the finishing flow ratio while ending the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 100% to 0% during the last loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the end of the spiral.

timelapse_type.label: Timelapse
timelapse_type.tooltip: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, a prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe the nozzle.

farthest_point_timelapse.label: Farthest point timelapse
farthest_point_timelapse.tooltip: When enabled, the timelapse snapshot is taken at the farthest point from camera instead of traveling to the wipe tower or excess chute. Only effective in traditional timelapse mode on non-I3 printers.

standby_temperature_delta.label: Temperature variation
standby_temperature_delta.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.

preheat_time.label: Preheat time
preheat_time.tooltip: To reduce the waiting time after tool change, Orca can preheat the next tool while the current tool is still in use. This setting specifies the time in seconds to preheat the next tool. Orca will insert a M104 command to preheat the tool in advance.

preheat_steps.label: Preheat steps
preheat_steps.tooltip: Insert multiple preheat commands (e.g. M104.1). Only useful for Prusa XL. For other printers, please set it to 1.

file_start_gcode.label: File header G-code
file_start_gcode.tooltip: G-code written at the very top of the output file, before any other content. Useful for adding metadata that printer firmware reads from the first lines of the file (e.g. estimated print time, filament usage). Supports placeholders like {print_time_sec} and {used_filament_length}.

machine_start_gcode.label: Start G-code
machine_start_gcode.tooltip: G-code added when starting a print.
machine_start_gcode.default_raw: "G28 ; home all axes\nG1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle\n"
machine_start_gcode.default:
G28 ; home all axes
G1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle

filament_start_gcode.label: Start G-code
filament_start_gcode.tooltip: G-code added when the printer starts using this filament

single_extruder_multi_material.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
single_extruder_multi_material.tooltip: Use single nozzle to print multi filament.

manual_filament_change.label: Manual Filament Change
manual_filament_change.tooltip: Enable this option to omit the custom Change filament G-code only at the beginning of the print. The tool change command (e.g., T0) will be skipped throughout the entire print. This is useful for manual multi-material printing, where we use M600/PAUSE to trigger the manual filament change action.

wipe_tower_type.label: Wipe tower type
wipe_tower_type.tooltip: Choose the wipe tower implementation for multi-material prints. Type 1 is recommended for Bambu and Qidi printers with a filament cutter. Type 2 offers better compatibility with multi-tool and MMU printers and provide overall better compatibility.

purge_in_prime_tower.label: Purge in prime tower
purge_in_prime_tower.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

tool_change_on_wipe_tower.label: Tool change on wipe tower
tool_change_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: Force the toolhead to travel to the wipe tower before issuing the tool change command (Tx). Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. By default Orca skips the travel on multi-toolhead machines because the firmware handles the head swap, which can result in the Tx command being issued above the printed part. Enable this option if you want the tool change to always be issued above the wipe tower instead.

wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers.label: No sparse layers (beta)
wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers.tooltip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no tool changes. On layers with a tool change, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

single_extruder_multi_material_priming.label: Prime all printing extruders
single_extruder_multi_material_priming.tooltip: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

toolchange_ordering.label: Toolchange ordering
toolchange_ordering.tooltip:
Determines the order of tool changes on each layer.
- Default: Starts with the last used extruder to minimize tool changes.
- Cyclic: Uses a fixed tool sequence each layer. This sacrifices speed for better surface quality, as the extra toolchanges allow layers more time to cool.

slice_closing_radius.label: Slice gap closing radius
slice_closing_radius.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

slicing_mode.label: Slicing Mode
slicing_mode.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

z_offset.label: Z offset
z_offset.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

support_type.label: Type
support_type.tooltip: Normal (auto) and Tree (auto) are used to generate support automatically. If Normal (manual) or Tree (manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated.

support_object_xy_distance.label: Support/object XY distance
support_object_xy_distance.tooltip: This controls the XY separation between an object and its support.

support_object_first_layer_gap.label: Support/object first layer gap
support_object_first_layer_gap.tooltip: XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.

support_angle.label: Pattern angle
support_angle.tooltip: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.

support_on_build_plate_only.label: On build plate only
support_on_build_plate_only.tooltip: This setting only generates supports that begin on the build plate.

support_critical_regions_only.label: Support critical regions only
support_critical_regions_only.tooltip: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

support_remove_small_overhang.label: Ignore small overhangs
support_remove_small_overhang.tooltip: Ignore small overhangs that possibly don't require support.

support_top_z_distance.label: Top Z distance
support_top_z_distance.tooltip: Z gap between the support\'s top and object.

support_bottom_z_distance.label: Bottom Z distance
support_bottom_z_distance.tooltip: Z gap between the object and the support bottom. If Support Top Z Distance is 0 and the bottom has interface layers, this value is ignored and the support is printed in direct contact with the object (no gap).

support_filament.label: Support/raft base
support_filament.tooltip:
Filament to print support base and raft.
"Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used.

support_interface_not_for_body.label: Avoid interface filament for base
support_interface_not_for_body.tooltip: Avoid using support interface filament to print support base if possible.

support_line_width.label: Support
support_line_width.tooltip: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

support_interface_loop_pattern.label: Loop pattern interface
support_interface_loop_pattern.tooltip: This covers the top contact layer of the supports with loops. It is disabled by default.

support_interface_filament.label: Support/raft interface
support_interface_filament.tooltip:
Filament to print support interface.
"Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used.

support_interface_top_layers.label: Top interface layers
support_interface_top_layers.tooltip: This is the number of top interface layers.

support_interface_spacing.label: Top interface spacing
support_interface_spacing.tooltip:
Spacing of interface lines. Zero means solid interface.
Force using solid interface when support ironing is enabled.

support_bottom_interface_spacing.label: Bottom interface spacing
support_bottom_interface_spacing.tooltip: This is the spacing of bottom interface lines. 0 means solid interface.

support_interface_speed.label: Support interface
support_interface_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for support interfaces.

support_base_pattern.label: Base pattern
support_base_pattern.tooltip:
Line pattern of support.

The Default option for Tree supports is Hollow, which means no base pattern. For other support types, the Default option is the Rectilinear pattern.

NOTE: For Organic supports, the two walls are supported only with the Hollow/Default base pattern. The Lightning base pattern is supported only by Tree Slim/Strong/Hybrid supports. For the other support types, the Rectilinear will be used instead of Lightning.

support_interface_pattern.label: Interface pattern
support_interface_pattern.tooltip: This is the line pattern for support interfaces. The default pattern for non-soluble support interfaces is Rectilinear while the default pattern for soluble support interfaces is Concentric.

support_base_pattern_spacing.label: Base pattern spacing
support_base_pattern_spacing.tooltip: This determines the spacing between support lines.

support_expansion.label: Normal support expansion
support_expansion.tooltip: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the horizontal span of normal support.

support_speed.label: Support
support_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for support.

support_style.label: Style
support_style.tooltip:
Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.
For tree support, slim and organic style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material (default organic), while hybrid style will create similar structure to normal support under large flat overhangs.

independent_support_layer_height.label: Independent support layer height
independent_support_layer_height.tooltip: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

support_threshold_angle.label: Threshold angle
support_threshold_angle.tooltip:
Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.
Note: If set to 0, normal supports use the Threshold overlap instead, while tree supports fall back to a default value of 30.

support_threshold_overlap.label: Threshold overlap
support_threshold_overlap.tooltip: If threshold angle is zero, support will be generated for overhangs whose overlap is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.

tree_support_branch_angle.label: Tree support branch angle
tree_support_branch_angle.tooltip: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

tree_support_branch_angle_organic.label: Tree support branch angle
tree_support_branch_angle_organic.tooltip: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

tree_support_angle_slow.label: Preferred Branch Angle
tree_support_angle_slow.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

tree_support_branch_distance.label: Tree support branch distance
tree_support_branch_distance.tooltip: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

tree_support_branch_distance_organic.label: Tree support branch distance
tree_support_branch_distance_organic.tooltip: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

tree_support_top_rate.label: Branch Density
tree_support_top_rate.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

tree_support_auto_brim.label: Auto brim width
tree_support_auto_brim.tooltip: Enabling this option means the width of the brim for tree support will be automatically calculated.

tree_support_brim_width.label: Tree support brim width
tree_support_brim_width.tooltip: Distance from tree branch to the outermost brim line.

tree_support_tip_diameter.label: Tip Diameter
tree_support_tip_diameter.tooltip: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

tree_support_branch_diameter.label: Tree support branch diameter
tree_support_branch_diameter.tooltip: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

tree_support_branch_diameter_angle.label: Branch Diameter Angle
tree_support_branch_diameter_angle.tooltip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

tree_support_branch_diameter_organic.label: Tree support branch diameter
tree_support_branch_diameter_organic.tooltip: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

tree_support_wall_count.label: Support wall loops
tree_support_wall_count.tooltip: This setting specifies the count of support walls in the range of [0,2]. 0 means auto.

tree_support_with_infill.label: Tree support with infill
tree_support_with_infill.tooltip: This setting specifies whether to add infill inside large hollows of tree support.

support_ironing.label: Ironing Support Interface
support_ironing.tooltip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of support interface again to make it more smooth. This setting controls whether support interface being ironed. When enabled, support interface will be extruded as solid too.

support_ironing_pattern.label: Support Ironing Pattern
support_ironing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

support_ironing_flow.label: Support Ironing flow
support_ironing_flow.tooltip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal support interface layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

support_ironing_spacing.label: Support Ironing line spacing
support_ironing_spacing.tooltip: This is the distance between the lines used for ironing.

activate_chamber_temp_control.label: Activate temperature control
activate_chamber_temp_control.tooltip:
Enable this option for automated chamber temperature control. This option activates the emitting of an M191 command before the "machine_start_gcode"
 which sets the chamber temperature and waits until it is reached. In addition, it emits an M141 command at the end of the print to turn off the chamber heater, if present.

This option relies on the firmware supporting the M191 and M141 commands either via macros or natively and is usually used when an active chamber heater is installed.

chamber_temperature.label: Chamber temperature
chamber_temperature.tooltip:
For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air filtration for ABS and ASA.

For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled (set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by material softening at the heat break.

If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]. This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed.

chamber_minimal_temperature.label: Minimal
chamber_minimal_temperature.tooltip:
This is the chamber temperature at which printing should start, while the chamber continues heating toward the "Target" chamber temperature. For example, set the Target to 60 and the Minimal to 50 to begin printing once the chamber reaches 50℃, without waiting for the full 60℃.

It sets a G-code variable named chamber_minimal_temperature, which can be passed to your print start macro or a heat soak macro, like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_MIN_TEMP=[chamber_minimal_temperature].

Unlike the "Target" chamber temperature, this option does not emit any M141/M191 commands; it only exposes the value to your custom G-code. It should not exceed the "Target" chamber temperature.

nozzle_temperature.label: Other layers
nozzle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature after the first layer

detect_thin_wall.label: Detect thin walls
detect_thin_wall.tooltip: This detects thin walls which can\u2019t contain two lines and uses a single line to print. It may not print as well because it\u2019s not a closed loop.

change_filament_gcode.label: Change filament G-code
change_filament_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when filament is changed, including T commands to trigger tool change.

change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code
change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed.

filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code (filament)
filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed for the active filament.

top_surface_line_width.label: Top surface
top_surface_line_width.tooltip: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

top_surface_speed.label: Top surface
top_surface_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for solid top surface infill.

top_shell_layers.label: Top shell layers
top_shell_layers.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than the top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased

top_shell_thickness.label: Top shell thickness
top_shell_thickness.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin a shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is determined simply by the number of top shell layers.

separated_infills.label: Separated infills
separated_infills.tooltip:
Centers the internal infill of each part on itself, as if it were sliced on its own, instead of on the whole assembly. Parts that touch or overlap are treated as one body and share a center; separate parts (or distinct 3D objects) each get their own.
Useful when an assembly groups several objects that should each keep a consistent, self-centered infill.
Affects line and grid patterns and rotation-template infills.
Patterns locked to global coordinates (Gyroid, Honeycomb, TPMS, ...) are unaffected.

center_of_surface_pattern.label: Center surface pattern on
center_of_surface_pattern.tooltip:
Chooses where the centering point of centered top/bottom surface patterns (Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral) is placed.
 - Each Surface: centers the pattern on every individual surface region, so each island is symmetric on its own.
 - Each Model: centers the pattern on each connected body. Parts that touch or overlap share one center; parts detached from the rest each get their own.
 - Each Assembly: uses a single shared center for the whole object or assembly.

travel_speed.label: Travel
travel_speed.tooltip: This is the speed at which traveling is done.

wipe.label: Wipe while retracting
wipe.tooltip: This moves the nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

wipe_distance.label: Wipe distance
wipe_distance.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

enable_prime_tower.label: Enable
enable_prime_tower.tooltip: The wiping tower can be used to clean up residue on the nozzle and stabilize the chamber pressure inside the nozzle in order to avoid appearance defects when printing objects.

prime_tower_enable_framework.label: Internal ribs
prime_tower_enable_framework.tooltip: Enable internal ribs to increase the stability of the prime tower.

flush_multiplier.label: Flush multiplier
flush_multiplier.tooltip: The actual flushing volumes is equal to the flush multiplier value multiplied by the flushing volumes in the table.

flush_multiplier_fast.label: Flush multiplier (Fast mode)
flush_multiplier_fast.tooltip: The flush multiplier used in fast purge mode.

prime_volume.label: Prime volume
prime_volume.tooltip: This is the volume of material to prime the extruder with on the tower.

prime_volume_mode.label: Prime volume mode
prime_volume_mode.tooltip: Selects how the wipe-tower prime and flush volumes are computed on multi-extruder printers.

prime_tower_width.label: Width
prime_tower_width.tooltip: This is the width of prime towers.

wipe_tower_rotation_angle.label: Wipe tower rotation angle
wipe_tower_rotation_angle.tooltip: Wipe tower rotation angle with respect to X axis.

prime_tower_brim_width.label: Brim width
prime_tower_brim_width.tooltip: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

wipe_tower_cone_angle.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
wipe_tower_cone_angle.tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

wipe_tower_max_purge_speed.label: Maximum wipe tower print speed
wipe_tower_max_purge_speed.tooltip:
The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

Increasing this speed may affect the tower's stability as well as increase the force with which the nozzle collides with any blobs that may have formed on the wipe tower.

Before increasing this parameter beyond the default of 90 mm/s, make sure your printer can reliably bridge at the increased speeds and that ooze when tool changing is well controlled.

For the wipe tower external perimeters the internal perimeter speed is used regardless of this setting.

wipe_tower_wall_type.label: Wall type
wipe_tower_wall_type.tooltip:
Wipe tower outer wall type.
1. Rectangle: The default wall type, a rectangle with fixed width and height.
2. Cone: A cone with a fillet at the bottom to help stabilize the wipe tower.
3. Rib: Adds four ribs to the tower wall for enhanced stability.

wipe_tower_extra_rib_length.label: Extra rib length
wipe_tower_extra_rib_length.tooltip: Positive values can increase the size of the rib wall, while negative values can reduce the size. However, the size of the rib wall can not be smaller than that determined by the cleaning volume.

wipe_tower_rib_width.label: Rib width
wipe_tower_rib_width.tooltip: Rib width is always less than half the prime tower side length.

wipe_tower_fillet_wall.label: Fillet wall
wipe_tower_fillet_wall.tooltip: The wall of prime tower will fillet.

wipe_tower_filament.label: Wipe tower
wipe_tower_filament.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

wiping_volumes_extruders.label: Purging volumes - load/unload volumes
wiping_volumes_extruders.tooltip: This vector saves required volumes to change from/to each tool used on the wipe tower. These values are used to simplify creation of the full purging volumes below.

prime_tower_skip_points.label: Skip points
prime_tower_skip_points.tooltip: The wall of prime tower will skip the start points of wipe path.

enable_tower_interface_features.label: Enable tower interface features
enable_tower_interface_features.tooltip: Enable optimized prime tower interface behavior when different materials meet.

enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_t.label: Cool down from interface boost during prime tower
enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_t.tooltip: When interface-layer temperature boost is active, set the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower so it cools down during the tower.

flush_into_infill.label: Flush into objects' infill
flush_into_infill.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects\' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be visible. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_support.label: Flush into objects' support
flush_into_support.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects\' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect unless a prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_objects.label: Flush into this object
flush_into_objects.tooltip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colors of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

wipe_tower_bridging.label: Maximal bridging distance
wipe_tower_bridging.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

wipe_tower_extra_spacing.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
wipe_tower_extra_spacing.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

wipe_tower_extra_flow.label: Extra flow for purging
wipe_tower_extra_flow.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

idle_temperature.label: Idle temperature
idle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups. This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

xy_hole_compensation.label: X-Y hole compensation
xy_hole_compensation.tooltip: Holes in objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the set value. Positive values make holes bigger and negative values make holes smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when objects have assembly issues.

xy_contour_compensation.label: X-Y contour compensation
xy_contour_compensation.tooltip: Contours of objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the set value. Positive values make contours bigger and negative values make contours smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when objects have assembly issues.

hole_to_polyhole.label: Convert holes to polyholes
hole_to_polyhole.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

hole_to_polyhole_threshold.label: Polyhole detection margin
hole_to_polyhole_threshold.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.label: Maximum Polyhole edge count
hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.tooltip:
Maximum number of polyhole edges
This setting limits the amount of edges a polyhole can have

thumbnails.label: G-code thumbnails
thumbnails.tooltip: Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

thumbnails_format.label: Format of G-code thumbnails
thumbnails_format.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware.

use_relative_e_distances.label: Use relative E distances
use_relative_e_distances.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option. Some extruders work better with this option unchecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked.

wall_generator.label: Wall generator
wall_generator.tooltip: The classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas, gap-fill is used. The Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width.

wall_transition_length.label: Wall transition length
wall_transition_length.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It\'s expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

wall_transition_filter_deviation.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
wall_transition_filter_deviation.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

wall_transition_angle.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
wall_transition_angle.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

wall_distribution_count.label: Wall distribution count
wall_distribution_count.tooltip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.

min_feature_size.label: Minimum feature size
min_feature_size.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

min_length_factor.label: Minimum wall length
min_length_factor.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

wall_maximum_resolution.label: Maximum wall resolution
wall_maximum_resolution.tooltip: This value determines the smallest wall line segment length in mm. The smaller you set this value, the more accurate and precise the walls will be.

wall_maximum_deviation.label: Maximum wall deviation
wall_maximum_deviation.tooltip: The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the 'Maximum wall resolution' setting. If you increase this, the print will be less accurate, but the G-Code will be smaller. 'Maximum wall deviation' limits 'Maximum wall resolution', so if the two conflict, 'Maximum wall deviation' takes precedence.

initial_layer_min_bead_width.label: First layer minimum wall width
initial_layer_min_bead_width.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

min_bead_width.label: Minimum wall width
min_bead_width.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

filament_change_length_nc.label: Hotend change
filament_change_length_nc.tooltip: When changing the hotend, it is recommended to extrude a certain length of filament from the original nozzle. This helps minimize nozzle oozing.

filament_ramming_travel_time.label: Extruder change
filament_ramming_travel_time.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle will perform a reverse travel movement for a certain period after the ramming is complete. The setting define the travel time.

filament_pre_cooling_temperature.label: Extruder change
filament_pre_cooling_temperature.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle temperature will be cooled during ramming. Therefore, the ramming time must be greater than the cooldown time. 0 means disabled.

filament_ramming_volumetric_speed.label: Extruder change
filament_ramming_volumetric_speed.tooltip: The maximum volumetric speed for ramming before extruder change, where -1 means using the maximum volumetric speed.

filament_ramming_travel_time_nc.label: Hotend change
filament_ramming_travel_time_nc.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle will perform a reverse travel movement for a certain period after the ramming is complete. The setting define the travel time.

filament_pre_cooling_temperature_nc.label: Hotend change
filament_pre_cooling_temperature_nc.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle temperature will be cooled during ramming. Note: only a cooldown command and fan activation are triggered, reaching the target temperature is not guaranteed. 0 means disabled.

filament_ramming_volumetric_speed_nc.label: Hotend change
filament_ramming_volumetric_speed_nc.tooltip: The maximum volumetric speed for ramming before a hotend change, where -1 means using the maximum volumetric speed.

filament_retract_length_nc.label: length when change hotend
filament_retract_length_nc.tooltip: When this retraction value is modified, it will be used as the amount of filament retracted inside the hotend before changing hotends.

support_fast_purge_mode.label: Support fast purge mode
support_fast_purge_mode.tooltip: Whether this printer supports fast purge mode with optimized temperature and multiplier.

filament_prime_volume.label: Filament change
filament_prime_volume.tooltip: The volume of material required to prime the extruder on the tower, excluding a hotend change.

filament_prime_volume_nc.label: Hotend change
filament_prime_volume_nc.tooltip: The volume of material required to prime the extruder for a hotend change on the tower.

filament_preheat_temperature_delta.label: Preheat temperature delta
filament_preheat_temperature_delta.tooltip: Temperature delta applied during pre-heating before tool change.

detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.label: Detect narrow internal solid infills
detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.tooltip: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.

export_3mf.label: Export 3MF
export_3mf.tooltip: This exports the project as a 3MF file.

export_slicedata.label: Export slicing data
export_slicedata.tooltip: Export slicing data to a folder

load_slicedata.label: Load slicing data
load_slicedata.tooltip: Load cached slicing data from directory.

export_stl.label: Export STL
export_stl.tooltip: Export the objects as single STL.

export_stls.label: Export multiple STLs
export_stls.tooltip: Export the objects as multiple STLs to directory.

slice.label: Slice
slice.tooltip: Slice the plates: 0-all plates, i-plate i, others-invalid

uptodate.label: UpToDate
uptodate.tooltip: Update the config values of 3MF to latest.

load_defaultfila.label: Load default filaments
load_defaultfila.tooltip: Load first filament as default for those not loaded.

mtcpp.label: mtcpp
mtcpp.tooltip: max triangle count per plate for slicing

mstpp.label: mstpp
mstpp.tooltip: max slicing time per plate in seconds

no_check.label: No check
no_check.tooltip: Do not run any validity checks, such as G-code path conflicts check.

export_settings.label: Export Settings
export_settings.tooltip: This exports settings to a file.

repetitions.label: Repetition count
repetitions.tooltip: Repetition count of the whole model.

ensure_on_bed.label: Ensure on bed
ensure_on_bed.tooltip: Lift the object above the bed when it is partially below. Disabled by default.

assemble.label: Assemble
assemble.tooltip: Arrange the supplied models in a plate and merge them in a single model in order to perform actions once.

rotate.label: Rotate
rotate.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Z axis in degrees.

rotate_x.label: Rotate around X
rotate_x.tooltip: Rotation angle around the X axis in degrees.

rotate_y.label: Rotate around Y
rotate_y.tooltip: Rotation angle around the Y axis in degrees.

scale.label: Scale per object
scale.tooltip:
Contains a string with the information about what scaling was applied to the individual objects. Indexing of the objects is zero-based (first object has index 0).
Example: 'x:100% y:50% z:100%'.

load_settings.label: Load General Settings
load_settings.tooltip: Load process/machine settings from the specified file.

load_filaments.label: Load Filament Settings
load_filaments.tooltip: Load filament settings from the specified file list.

skip_objects.label: Skip Objects
skip_objects.tooltip: Skip some objects in this print.

clone_objects.label: Clone Objects
clone_objects.tooltip: Clone objects in the load list.

uptodate_settings.label: Load uptodate process/machine settings when using uptodate
uptodate_settings.tooltip: load up-to-date process/machine settings from the specified file when using up-to-date

uptodate_filaments.label: Load uptodate filament settings when using uptodate
uptodate_filaments.tooltip: Load uptodate filament settings from the specified file when using uptodate.

downward_check.label: Downward machines check
downward_check.tooltip: If enabled, check whether current machine downward compatible with the machines in the list.

downward_settings.label: Downward machines settings
downward_settings.tooltip: The machine settings list needs to do downward checking.
